passage:
When Sara visited her aunt, she found a small music box on the shelf. It was dusty and did not open easily.
Her aunt said the music box had belonged to Sara's great-grandmother. When Sara turned the key, the song came out slowly, with a few missing notes.
"It sounds broken," Sara said.
"Yes," her aunt answered, "but I still know the song."
Then her aunt began to hum along. The missing notes did not matter because she remembered them.
Sara listened quietly. She understood that some objects are not kept because they work perfectly. They are kept because they help people remember what time has taken away.
